issues.legal_issue: A divorce decree may be granted on the parties’ joint request where their marriage has irretrievably broken down and they have agreed on the terms of the decree.
material_facts: The parties had been living separately for more than three years, and the Court found no chance of their coming together.
Both parties jointly requested a divorce and placed their written request on the record.
They agreed on the allocation of shares in a plot, delivery of its title deed, and the petitioner’s waiver of maintenance claims for herself and their son.
A divorce petition filed by the respondent was pending before the Family Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court granted a divorce decree on the agreed terms and disposed of the pending divorce petition accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on its power to do complete justice between the parties, finding that the marriage had irretrievably broken down and that there was no prospect of reconciliation. The order cites no statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: divorce_proceeding and parties_living_separately and marriage_irretrievably_broken and joint_divorce_request and agreed_decree_terms

predicates.divorce_proceeding: The matter concerns a proceeding seeking dissolution of a marriage.
predicates.marriage_irretrievably_broken: The court found that the marriage had irretrievably broken down and that the spouses had no prospect of coming together.
predicates.joint_divorce_request: Both spouses jointly asked the court to grant a divorce.
predicates.agreed_decree_terms: The spouses agreed on terms to govern the divorce decree.

issues.definition: When a divorce proceeding involves spouses living separately, a marriage found irretrievably broken, a joint request for divorce, and agreed decree terms, the rule provides for a divorce decree on those terms.
